subject: User selects nothing but the app does select

messages.author: f912724b32d84d06
messages.subject: User selects nothing but the app does select
parts:
Hello!

My user reads in a data frame and then has to select certain column names as different inputs for my algorithm - from among all the column names in my data frame.

In one case I want the user to EITHER select one column name or select nothing.
If I run my app without selecting anything as 'Column with Weights' - it automatically picks the name of the very first column and runs with it. In my code below I said selected = NULL, but it doesn't seem to work. Any advice?
Thanks a lot!

      output$Weightvariable <- renderUI({
            if(is.null(input$datafile)){return()}
            weightvar <- names(mydata()$df.raw)
            selectInput('Weightvariable', 'Column with Weights', choices = weightvar,
                        selected = NULL, multiple = FALSE)
      })

messages.author: eb0a34481312005c
messages.subject: Re: User selects nothing but the app does select
parts:
This is the expected behavior for `selectInput`. If you read the help file for the function it says : If not specified then defaults to the first value for single-select lists and no values for multiple select lists. When `selected = NULL` it will always use the first column if you don't specify otherwise. If you want "nothing" as your first choice you could have something like:
 
weightvar <- c("",names(mydata()$df.raw))

Best,
M.

messages.subject: Re: User selects nothing but the app does select
parts:
Thank you very much!
First I thought this solution should do the trick, but I got an error I wasn't getting before:

Error in `[.data.frame`(data, data[[v]] == 1, c(data.variables, "mywgt")) : 
  undefined columns selected

It happened because inside my "server.r" script I have the following main function:

out <- calcMDscores(data = mydata()$df.raw, util.vars = utilvars, weight.var = wgtvar,
                                filter.vars = filtervars, items.per.task = nr.per.task)

This function DOES accept NULL as an input for weight.var (weight.var = NULL). In fact, it's a default. But now we are basically telling it: weight.var = "". And it got confused. So, I had to add before that:

            if(input$Weightvariable == "") {wgtvar <- NULL} else {
            wgtvar <- input$Weightvariable }

Now it's working.
Thank you again!
